failure_summary.description: Agents omitted or misread latest-turn actions, including attraction requests and explicit proximity relations.
Agents used stale or less-refined results, repeated covered criteria, or searched when a compatible result was cached.
Agents used unsupported or incorrectly encoded fields and added unstated filters or cross-domain preferences.

patch.reasoning: Clarify that an attraction request remains actionable even when it does not imply proximity, make explicit “near” relations translate into nearest-results calls rather than neighborhood filters, and reinforce omission of unstated options and separation of domain-specific constraints. Existing cache guidance already covers cache selection and refinement, so it is not duplicated.

edits.insert_after: Interest in visiting or dining at a place alone does not imply a proximity request or require a nearest-results call.
edits.content: - This no-nearest rule does not cancel an attraction request: when the user wants to visit a named attraction, retrieve a compatible result for that exact name or search with `attraction_name`; include an explicitly stated attraction `type` as well. A generic or category-only attraction result does not cover a separately named site.

edits.insert_after: - Pass the relevant result objects for the two domains being compared. Set `groupBy` to the domain whose candidates the user wants ranked or recommended (the focal domain), not the reference domain: hotels near an attraction use `groupBy="hotel"`, while restaurants near a hotel use `groupBy="restaurant"`.
edits.content: - For an explicit request for hotels or restaurants near a named attraction, treat “near” as a cross-domain relation: do not pass the attraction name as a hotel or restaurant `neighborhood`. Ensure the exact attraction result is available, then call `search_nearest` with both relevant results and the requested focal domain.

edits.replace: Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
edits.content: Carry forward relevant details from the conversation and include explicitly supplied criteria in the appropriate call. Send only schema-supported parameters; do not infer amenities, ratings, or other preferences. Omit optional fields the user did not state rather than setting them to `False`. Keep each constraint attached to its stated domain; for example, a flight budget is not a hotel budget. Do not infer exact party or room counts from broad descriptions such as “family.” Treat “solo” as one traveler only when a supported traveler-count field is available; do not infer a room count from it. A traveler count is not a flight-search parameter unless the schema provides one.
